issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: four unrelated features crammed into a single diff
issues.detail: This patch does four distinct things: table variable indexes in DECLARE, CREATE LOGIN identifier/nstring tweaks, negative IDENTITY seed, and ALTER TABLE multi-DROP refactor. Each lands cleanly on its own and each can break independently. A maintainer six years from now bisecting a regression in IDENTITY parsing will curse the author for having to untangle it from the CREATE LOGIN changes. Split it.

issues.description: AlterTable lost the Delimited() wrapper - multiple comma-separated alterations no longer parse
issues.detail: The original grammar wrapped the OneOf in Delimited(...), which is how real T-SQL ALTER TABLE statements with multiple actions parse (e.g. the deleted fixture `ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c`). The new grammar drops Delimited() entirely. That existing test case was silently deleted from alter_table.sql to make the new grammar pass instead of fixing the grammar. This is a regression dressed up as a refactor - real ALTER TABLE supports comma-delimited actions per MS docs, and the test that proved it was removed rather than preserved.

issues.description: PR description admits the deleted fixture was 'invalid' without citation
issues.detail: The description says 'Removed invalid delimited section in alter table and invalid alter table example' with no link to MS docs proving it. T-SQL ALTER TABLE absolutely supports comma-separated ADD/DROP actions in many cases. Either cite the doc that says the deleted example is invalid, or restore the Delimited wrapper. 'Trust me, it was invalid' is not a review-able claim.

issues.description: BAD-TASTE: SignedSegmentGrammar repeated twice instead of factoring a signed numeric literal
issues.detail: IdentityGrammar now reads `SignedSegmentGrammar(optional), NumericLiteralSegment, Comma, SignedSegmentGrammar(optional), NumericLiteralSegment`. The same pattern - optional sign followed by a number - is going to show up everywhere T-SQL allows negative numerics (DEFAULT values, CHECK constraints, etc). Either introduce a SignedNumericLiteralSegment helper or accept that this will get copy-pasted forever. Not a blocker, but the next person who needs negative literals will not find this pattern and will reinvent it.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepting NumericLiteralSegment is suspicious without a source
issues.detail: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE values are language names (lcid integers via sp_configure, but in CREATE LOGIN they're identifiers or strings per MS docs - 'us_english', N'us_english'). Adding NumericLiteralSegment to the OneOf may be legal in some form, but the PR provides no test case for it and no MS doc reference. Either add a fixture exercising the numeric form or drop that branch.

issues.description: Test fixture for new declare-table-index case is missing a statement terminator
issues.detail: `declare @var table (...) ` has no semicolon at the end. Matches the rest of the file's loose style, but worth a note - the surrounding fixtures are inconsistent about terminators and this adds another one. Minor.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The individual parser additions are reasonable in shape - table-index in DECLARE, negative IDENTITY seed, naked identifiers in CREATE LOGIN, nstring passwords - and the fixtures cover them. But this is THREE-PATCHES (really four) submitted as one, which is hostile to bisect and review. More seriously, the ALTER TABLE refactor drops the outer Delimited() wrapper and deletes a working test case that exercised comma-separated ADD/DROP actions, with the PR description hand-waving it as 'invalid' without citation. That's a regression masquerading as cleanup. Split the patch, restore the deleted ALTER TABLE fixture or cite the MS doc that says it's invalid, then resubmit.
